principles: Implementation may proceed in parallel, but capability proof and claim unlock remain sequential.
Fail closed when lower-layer proof, authority evidence, or shared schema is missing or stale.
Keep Parallel Development thin: coordination protocol, not a new capability layer or product claim.
Only fix real correctness issues; do not optimize or split work arbitrarily.
drivers: User needs a go/blocked decision before launching four parallel Baseline 2-5 workstreams.
Current authority docs keep CLI as thin local/shadow client and forbid L2+ receipt claims.
Current baseline_run surface does not yet expose ENG/UDM/SAFE/CLAIM runner IDs, so implementation readiness must be audited before coding claims.

options.name: A: coordination audit first, then parallel implementation only if gates are clear
pros: Directly resolves product-reviewer advisory by producing a user-visible go/blocked decision.
Prevents schema drift across Engineering, Loop, Production Safety, and Claim workstreams.
Preserves sequential proof and fail-closed claim lock.
cons: Delays immediate coding by one story.
May produce BLOCKED if runner source or Layer 1 proof is insufficient.

options.name: B: start four implementation workstreams immediately
pros: Agents can discover gaps while coding.
cons: Risks each line inventing a different artifact schema or authority boundary.
Could create false capability claim before lower layers pass.
Does not answer the user-visible go/blocked question first.

options.name: C: serialize all Baseline 2-5 implementation
pros: Minimizes merge conflicts and coordination overhead.
Simpler to audit one line at a time.
cons: Leaves available host parallelism unused even when write scopes can be separated.
Conflates implementation order with proof order and slows safe development unnecessarily.

chosen: A: coordination audit first, then parallel implementation only if gates are clear
rationale: 选择 A，因为当前任务的真实用户价值是先给出可审计的 go/blocked 判定，并冻结共享契约与 ownership，之后才能安全并行写代码；直接并行实现会放大 false claim 和 schema drift 风险。

preMortem.trigger: Layer 1 baseline suite fails or lacks independent review evidence but the coordination artifact still says parallel coding may start.
preMortem.consequence: Lattice begins higher-layer work on an unproven foundation and later capability claims become misleading.
preMortem.mitigation: Record Layer 1 as blocked/not_authorized unless local evidence and independent review evidence both exist and match current material hash.

preMortem.trigger: Engineering, Loop, Production Safety, or Claim agents define their own final-report/baseline-suite/claim-report fields.
preMortem.consequence: Integration becomes subjective and claim evaluator cannot mechanically compare artifacts.
preMortem.mitigation: Freeze shared contract and ownership before dispatch; any schema change requires coordinator review and sequential gate update.

preMortem.trigger: A local/shadow or transport-accepted report is treated as receipt-backed L2+ authority evidence.
preMortem.consequence: Production Safety or Capability Claim claims more than Lattice can prove.
preMortem.mitigation: Use canonical authorityMode/evidenceClass and keep authority.receiptVerified=false, productionDone=false, authorityChanged=false, receiptRefs=[] unless verified receipt-backed path exists.

preMortem.trigger: Multiple agents edit shared gates/schema/validator files simultaneously.
preMortem.consequence: One workstream silently overwrites another or bypasses a lower-layer proof condition.
preMortem.mitigation: Ownership map must assign disjoint ownedPaths; shared files are read-only unless an explicit merge-queue change is approved.
